IREN Rating: Outperform  Target Price: 55.00 USDIREN remains misunderstood and
the victim of the recent ‘offensive’ Neocloud label. There maybe over 200+
neoclouds who sell compute collateralising GPUs as their sole physical asset.
Neoclouds as defined today face long term lease commitments (10-15 years) and
debt repayments, while selling compute over shorter horizons (short term spot
contracts to multi-year term contracts). This mismatch creates financial
uncertainty and potential liquidity challenges, when you combine debt funded
capex & leases should the GPU compute prices suffer. IREN’s business model is
based on self-owned unencumbered physical power assets with the flexibility to
decide the pace of development, leverage profile and optimise compute pricing
to benefit from movements in spot pricing. IREN is not sold out for the next 2
years at suboptimal historical pricing - IREN has over ~1.4GW of approved
capacity to sell (over 5GW grid connected sites), while the compute markets
remain tight with political headwinds and the option to pace capex, should the
financing markets remain challenging. And the skeptics are missing a big part
of the financing equation - prepayments. On a recent contract, IREN reported
90% prepayments with 45-50% prepayments being the norm for any new compute

# Airbnb

## Growth Mode and Share Gains

  
---  
  
By Doug Anmuth

ABNB, ABNB US  
Price (05 Nov 26):$170.13  
**▲** Price Target (Dec-27):$202.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$170.00  
  
ABNB shares traded up +11% post-close w/strong execution driving upside to 3Q
results & the full year outlook. ABNB delivered its fastest revenue growth in
over 3 years, w/acceleration across the business including both core &
expansion markets. Every region delivered DD% nights growth in 3Q & North
America grew at the fastest pace in four years. While underlying global travel
demand remains healthy, ABNB’s execution across product & growth
initiatives—spurred by AI—have been key to driving strong performance. After
years of work rebuilding the tech stack, redesigning the app, & improving the
core experience, AI is enabling ABNB to build, test, & iterate on products at
an accelerated pace. Notably, Reserve Now, Pay Later drove a 3%pt lift to 3Q
nights growth & is supporting lead time expansion & higher priced bookings.
ABNB now expects mid-teens% GBV growth & high-teens% revenue growth for the
full year, & Adj. EBITDA margin of 36%. Looking ahead, ABNB is focused on
executing on a robust product roadmap in 2027 to continue its momentum. In
1H27, ABNB plans to begin rolling out its own specialized AI agent, which mgmt
believes will be superior to general agents for complex tasks like travel. The
agent will leverage ABNB’s 20 years of data & expertise, build custom
generative UIs, & integrate with external MCPs. We remain encouraged by ABNB’s
strong execution & compounding AI-driven product innovation, & our Nights,
GBV, revenue, & Adj. EBITDA come up 2-3% in 2026E & 0-3% in 2027E. Our
December 2027 PT of $202 based on ~16x our ’28E FCF, and we remain Neutral-
rated while looking for a better entry point and durability of execution.

  * Strong Execution Drives Upside to 3Q Results & Outlook. ABNB’s 3Q N&S booked (+16% Y/Y to 155M), GBV (+21% Y/Y to $27.7B), revenue (+19% Y/Y to $4.9B), & Adj. EBITDA ($2.5B, 52% margin) were all ahead of expectations. Every region delivered DD% nights growth, with acceleration across nearly all expansion markets, as well as all five core markets. In addition to healthy underlying travel demand, N&S benefited from continued product momentum including Reserve Now, Pay Later, which contributed a 3%pt lift to 3Q N&S. The 4Q revenue guide of $3.22B-$3.28B (+16%-18%, or +14%-16% FXN) implys high teens revenue growth for the full year (vs. prior mid-teens%+), reflecting continued execution & resilient travel demand, though ABNB is closely monitoring ongoing developments in EMEA. On profits, ABNB raised the full-year Adj. EBITDA margin guide to 36% (vs. prior 35.5%) driven by ongoing cost discipline & AI-driven efficiencies, but still expects Y/Y margin compression in 4Q due to the timing of marketing spend. Looking ahead, mgmt is focused on continuing to execute across a robust product roadmap to drive continued durable growth & believes the company has demonstrated the ability to reinvest upside to support continued momentum. 
  * AI Innovation Continues. ABNB continues to leverage AI to accelerate the pace of innovation & in 3Q shipped 50+ products and features, ~70% more than a year ago. Additionally, ABNB’s AI assistant is now available in 50+ languages & drove customer support cost down -17% Y/Y in 3Q, with ~40% of all customer support issues solved without a human agent (up from ~33% in 2Q). Importantly, ABNB is building its own specialized agent & expects to begin rolling the product out in 1H27. Mgmt believes that specialized agents will be superior to general agents in handling complex tasks like travel planning & booking, w/ABNB maintaining three distinct advantages: 1) Deep understanding of both sides of its marketplace, w/20 years of experience supporting how people search, book, & host; 2) ABNB’s role in the reservation extends beyond just the booking, & includes payments, customer support, etc; & 3) ABNB is building a custom designed, AI-native interface specifically for travel that will draw on hundreds of travel specific components incl maps, photos, itineraries, etc. to match customers with what they are looking for.
  * Other Notable Points. 1)First-time booker growth accelerated to +13% Y/Y, with Gen Z growing the fastest & acceleration in many of ABNB’s largest markets; 2) ABNB repurchased ~$700M shares in 3Q & announced a new authorization to repurchase an additional $12B on top of the remaining $2.7B from the existing authorization; 3) By region, North America grew LDD%, EMEA grew mid-teens%, & LATAM/APAC both grew over 20%, an acceleration across all four regions relative to 2Q; 4) Nights booked on the app increased +29% & accounted for 66% of total nights booked (vs. 62% in 3Q25); 5) While Hotels remain a SD% of total nights booked, it is growing faster than the core business & mgmt believes it can generate multiple billions of dollars from hotels in the coming years without needing significant market share; 6) 3Q take rate was down slightly Y/Y driven by the expansion of Reserve Now, Pay Later, partially offset by travel insurance & the single service fee, which ABNB expects to support a modest increase in take rate over time.

# Cloudflare

## F3Q26 Review: Acceleration in Growth and Stellar Customer Momentum KPIs
Increase Visibility into Higher Structural Growth; Reiterate OW

  
---  
  
By Samik Chatterjee, CFA
AC,
Jaiden R
Patel,
Mashu
Nishi

Click here for the full document and
disclaimers

| Overweight  
---  
NET, NET US  
Price (05 Nov 26):$244.51  
**▲** Price Target (Dec-27):$375.00  
Prior (Dec-27):$350.00  
  
Cloudflare delivered another quarter, bearing proof to the thesis that the
structural growth rate for the company is higher with AI driving demand for
products across Acts I -III, even as the company already booked initial
revenues for Act IV, which the company expects will ramp over time to exceed
the magnitude of revenue from the other Acts. The quarter marked a double-
digit sequential revenue growth of 12% from F2Q, ahead of the typical
sequential growth rates in the range of 4%-10% over the last couple of years,
and also supported a much stronger revenue beat in the quarter compared to the
typical magnitude. While momentum was strong across the portfolio, the primary
driver of the stronger-than-typical beat and strong growth metrics was
variable revenue led by consumption, which is now tracking closer to mid-teens
of revenue. NRR accelerated to 122%, showcasing increasing momentum with
existing customers, as well as the sequential addition of 158K customers,
tracking at almost 2x the pace of new customer adds in F2Q. The wins announced
by Cloudflare highlighted the increasing momentum of attach of Zero Trust
security as well as attach of Workers, evidencing the flywheel of growth from
a stack running across Acts I-III. In relation to Act IV, the company outlined
initial revenues being recorded from the cooperation with OpenAI to optimize
web crawling, providing visibility into the returns from the product to
customers, even as the company continues to make progress towards material
monetization of microtransactions in relation to the interaction between
content providers and agents. The acceleration in the momentum increases our
confidence in the TAM expansion as well as the higher share of wins relative
to competition across products, supporting our outlook for robust and
accelerating growth in the out-years and expectations of stronger earnings and
free cash flow growth helped by leverage on the robust revenue growth. The
acceleration is putting the company in a position to achieve GAAP income
profitability in 4Q FY26, well ahead of its initial target for FY28, and in a
position for significant positive revisions to its long-term targets. We are
raising our revenue and profit forecasts, as well as our Dec-27 price target
to $375 (from $350 prior).

  * F3Q26 (Sep-end) Results: Broad-based variable consumption demand and operating leverage drove a record quarter, with accelerating Workers and agentic workloads, large-customer expansion, and strong GTM execution. Revenue tracked to $783M or +39% y/y, ahead of JPMe at $747M and consensus of $742M and the guidance range of $736M-$737M.  The revenue outperformance was driven by rapid expansion in variable consumption workloads, continued momentum among large customers, and broad-based go-to-market execution. Cloudflare added more than 158K paying customers during the quarter, nearly double the previous record of more than 80K in F2Q and saw record y/y net additions across all large customer annualized revenue cohorts.  While RPO growth of +34% y/y decelerated in F3Q from +38% y/y last quarter, cRPO accelerated to +37% y/y compared to 34% y/y last quarter. For a second consecutive quarter, NRR increased by 2 points sequentially to now 122%, reaching a four-year record. While gross margin of 72% came in slightly below JPMe and consensus at 73%, PF operating profit came in ahead at $137M relative to the guidance mid-point as well as JPMe and consensus at ~$130M, with PF operating margin landing in-line with the guide. Workers’ growth is supporting operating margin expansion, with lower cost to book. PF EPS of $0.38 was ahead of the $0.34 guide for F3Q and JPMe/consensus of $0.34/$0.35.
  * F4Q26 (Dec-end) Guidance: Revenue outlook is well ahead of expectations, sustaining high-30s growth as strong demand and improving execution support earlier GAAP profitability. Cloudflare provided F4Q revenue guidance of $845M-$846M, with the midpoint ahead of JPMe and consensus of $805M and $799M, respectively. The guidance implies revenue growth of +38% y/y vs. JPMe/consensus at +33%/+32%. Management notes that the F4Q guidance framework is supported by a long tail of customers, rather than being concentrated among a few. Cloudflare guided PF operating income of $156M-$157M, representing a PF operating margin of 19%, which is in-line with JPMe and ahead of consensus at 18%. Workers’ growth and improving compute efficiency are supporting operating leverage and the expectation of GAAP profitability in F4Q, well ahead of the company’s prior target by FY28. PF EPS guidance of $0.43 is also ahead of JPMe of $0.39 and consensus of $0.38.
  * FY26 (Dec-end) Guidance: Outlook edges higher more than the F3Q revenue beat, reiterates network CapEx target. Revenue increased by $97M at the midpoint (relative to the $46M 3Q beat) to $3B vs. JPMe and consensus of $2.9B. The guidance now implies revenue growth of 37% compared to JPMe of 33%, consensus of 32%, and the prior outlook of 32%.  PF operating income was revised to $462M-$463M vs. $443M-$444M prior, ahead of JPMe and consensus at $451M and $446M, respectively. Cloudflare raised the PF EPS target to $1.35 relative, an increase of nearly $0.10 and higher than JPMe/consensus of $1.27. The company reiterated its full-year network CapEx of 14-15% of revenue. 
  * Key notes from the call back (please reach out for more detailed notes). Variable consumption was mid-teens of revenue pool-of-funds was low-double-digit. Cloudflare reiterated its historical guidance philosophy heading into next year, as well as a likely need to take a holistic view to updating guidance on the next print on account of meeting most targets well ahead of earlier plans.

Erik W Woodring, Dylan Liu, Maya C Neuman, Rauf Ural  
November 6, 2026  
---  
| | | STX fundamentals remain strong – revs/pricing are accelerating, supply/demand gap is widening, and buybacks could reach ~30% of mkt cap in 2.5 years. Yet shares trade at just 5x our CY28 EPS (or ~3x our bull-case). We address 5 key debates and 3 factors for re-rating once the storm passes; Top Pick.   
---  
| | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * No signs of HDD industry irrationality – unit capacity stays disciplined, while supply growth remains driven by areal density gains. 
  * While component inflation slows cost-downs, stronger pricing should offset cost pressure and continue the margin expansion trajectory. 
  * HAMR remains on track with no technical qualification issues; rising HAMR mix supports ~25% EB CAGR target without adding HDD units. 
  * HDDs are less cyclical than memory, with growth more EB-driven and far lower capital intensity and fixed-cost leverage than NAND/DRAM. 
  * A•Areal density + mix shift towards data center are structurally lifting HDD margins, supporting higher through-cycle earnings and multiples than history. 

  
  
We walk away from our 3-day roadshow with STX CFO Gianluca Romano and Head of
IR Shanye Hudson with more conviction in our OW thesis – what’s the path
forward? Over the last 3 months, STX shares are down 43% (and 59% off 52 week
highs) while our FY27/FY28 EPS estimates have moved 25-50% higher – leaving
shares trading at 5.2x our CY28 EPS of $89.21 and 3.4x our bull-case CY28 EPS
(which embeds pricing from our June Taiwan checks) – below historical trough
multiples for HDDs (Exhibit 1). While higher rates and questions about capex
spend/financing have driven the bulk of this de-rating, concerns about HDD
industry rationality have caused a disconnect between HDD’s and other AI capex
bottlenecks in the last month, with HDD’s underperforming memory, semi-cap,
compute, and optical by 5pts in the month of October, despite strong earnings
results. However, our roadshow with STX mgmt this week reinforced the strength
of this story – AI tailwinds to HDD demand are still very early innings but
are helping to accelerate EB demand leaving the supply/demand gap wider today
than 3 months ago, pricing is also accelerating and more than offsetting
component cost inflation to drive strengthening incremental margins, customer
visibility is improving/elongating, HAMR commercialization and qualifications
are progressing as-scheduled, and with FCF growing each quarter, STX should be
able to buyback ~30% of the company in the next 2-2.5 years.

We appreciate that there are a number of broader AI/data center concerns that
are impacting AI bottlenecks, and as long as we are in an environment
characterized by fear and uncertainty, HDDs are going to underperform, even at
sub-trough valuations. However, we remain steadfast that fundamentals are
robust, any potential DC build delays would do little to impact our model
given HDD demand is far outpacing supply, these stocks are cheap even on
Street EPS (we are 13-15% above Consensus), and mgmt sounds convicted.
Therefore, once this fear and uncertainty subsides, STX (and HDDs more
broadly) should be amongst the first AI winners investors return to, and we
reiterate our OW rating.

STX is now trading at 6x/7x our/Consensus FY28 EPS, which is below/near the
historical trough multiple of 8x despite strengthening earnings outlook.
 Source: Company data,
FactSet, Morgan Stanley Research  
---  
  
_Below, we leverage our management meetings to answer 5 of the markets most
pressing questions (including market rationality), and then highlight 3 facts
we believe can help to shift the narrative towards HDD multiple expansion._

1\. What happened with Nearline EB growth in the Sept/Dec qtrs, and what’s the
message on LT EB growth, demand, and customer visibility? September quarter
nearline EBs were up just 2% Q/Q as a result of two factors: STX (1) over-
indexed supply towards enterprise OEM customers that historically buy lower
capacity drives than CSPs, and (2) staged (i.e. prepared) 40TB HAMR drives in
anticipation of major hyperscaler customer qualifications being completed
beyond the September quarter. In our meetings, mgmt made clear land, power,
shell/data center readiness was not an issue, nor were there any technical
challenges with HAMR quals – the slower Q/Q EB growth in September was
entirely mix and timing related. As a result, nearline EB growth will re-
accelerate in the December quarter (both Q/Q and Y/Y). As mgmt framed it –
their December quarter revenue guide implies $600M of Q/Q growth, but in
contrast to the September quarter, EB growth will be a greater Q/Q contributor
of revenue growth relative to pricing as 40TB Mosaic 4 volumes ramp.

More importantly, STX sees no evidence that underlying demand is weakening. In
fact, mgmt made clear hyperscaler EB demand is running “well above” STX's ~25%
long-term annual EB growth framework, while visibility remains strong and
continues to elongate. Consistent with what mgmt has been saying, STX has
relatively precise product/mix visibility over the next 4 quarters, with both
volume and pricing negotiated for CY27, and only EB’s committed into
CY28/CY29. In the coming months, STX will start negotiating pricing for CY28
amidst an even tighter supply/demand and inflationary component cost
environment, which to us implies only stronger pricing into 2028 (even if NAND
prices fall). Taken together, (1) the September quarter EB growth decel looks
more like a timing/mix quarter than a reversal of the HDD cycle, with Dec
representing the next leg of EB acceleration, and (2) medium-to-long-term
demand trends are improving, with supply still the gating factor, helping to
elongate the HDD cycle.

2\. Is there any evidence of industry irrationality impacting HDD supply
growth or pricing? The short and very clear answer is no. Despite investor
concerns around incremental industry capacity following misleading headlines a
month ago (see
here,
here,
and
here),
STX sees rational supply behavior in the industry and has no plans to add
incremental unit capacity, maintaining capex at 4-6% of revenue as has been
the case for years. Mgmt reiterated that it targets to achieve ~25% annual EB
growth primarily through areal density gains (i.e. mix to higher-capacity HAMR
drives) – again, a consistent message – while keeping physical unit growth
roughly flat. And while some investors may question the additional equipment
investments and reasons for STX purchasing external PMR heads, these are
initiatives intended to support HAMR EB growth that requires more heads, more
platters, and a longer production cycle time. Expanding unit capacity is not
in the cards.

The broader industry rationality message also remains constructive. Mgmt sees
competitors as similarly focused on technology-driven EB growth – not
capturing unit share – and lower-end competition remains constrained by a lack
of vertical integration (and not enough capex at critical suppliers to support
non-vertically integrated competitors doubling capacity) and leading edge
technology, where STX is 3-4+ years ahead. Importantly, industry pricing is
also very rational, despite concerns to the contrary – lower-end competitors
are not making headway in gaining share; they remain the distant third source.
And given the supply/demand imbalance in HDD’s, there are no examples of
competition using pricing to capture demand. In fact, our checks would suggest
lower-end competitors are sometimes more price aggressive to the upside. All
told, we remain encouraged that we see no evidence of industry competitors
reverting to the prior playbook of prioritizing share gains over
profitability, and we expect this landscape to persist.

3\. How should we model Cost/TB given component cost pressure, and what does
this mean for HDD pricing and margins? The message from mgmt is that the
current MSD% Y/Y cost/TB declines should persist for a few quarters. The cost
of internally manufactured heads and media continues to decline, and as mix
shifts to higher capacity HAMR drives continues, cost/TB declines should
remain robust (i.e. going from a 30TB to 40TB HDD lowers cost/TB by 25%, all
else equal). However, there is upward cost pressure from externally purchased
components, including DRAM, NAND, SoCs, controllers, electronics and
mechanical components. And as STX has worked down lower-cost inventory, this
component inflation is having a more pronounced offset to the tailwinds listed
above. This implies a shallower cost-down trajectory this year, rather than a
deterioration in STX's underlying technology cost curve, though STX mgmt noted
that they expect external component costs to “rise, stabilize, and then fall
again” (no timeline attached to this comment).

Importantly, STX incorporates expected component cost inflection when
negotiating pricing. This was one reason why nearline price/TB accelerated in
the September quarter, resulting in even stronger incremental margins in the
September quarter vs. June, despite the shallower Cost/TB trajectory. Mgmt
indicated future pricing will continue to embed changes to its cost structure,
though as we noted earlier, pricing will also incorporate the added value of
delivering higher capacity drives and a favorable supply/demand environment.
In our view, this should reaffirm that Y/Y pricing growth should generally
accelerate through CY27 and into CY28, consistent with our checks.

4\. Are there any issues with HAMR qualifications, and how does growing HAMR
mix impact STX EB growth and competition? No. Mozaic 4 is already shipping at
STX's 2 largest cloud customers, and additional qualifications with other
large hyperscalers and enterprise OEMs is progressing normally, with quals
still lasting a standard 6-9 months. STX expects a number of these additional
customers to complete Mozaic 4 qualifications this quarter, which alongside
greater head and media production will support HAMR reaching 50% of nearline
EBs shipped and 40TB HAMR products surpassing 50% of HAMR mix exiting this
quarter. Beyond Mosaic 4, STX expects to begins 5TB/platter HAMR
qualifications towards the end of CY27, which means 50TB/drive shipments
should commence in C2H28, and has already successfully reached 8TB/platter
technology in the lab, with lab to commercialization typically taking 3-4
years. This compares favorably to competitors without comparable areal density
progress that are likely to face eventual physical limitations on capacity per
drive. HAMR success therefore represents the strongest path towards ~25% long-
term EB growth while likely widening STX’s technology advantage as smaller
competitors work to qualify/ship 2 generations old technology.

5\. When should we expect buybacks to step-up, and how much stock could STX
buy back in the next 2-3 years? In the last 12 months, STX has reduced gross
debt outstanding from $5.0B to $2.8B and retired 100% of their previously
dilutive convertible debt. Mgmt made clear these targeted efforts to improve
B/S quality are now complete, and attention is shifting towards capital
return, where returning 75% of FCF to shareholders is still the stated goal,
but “opportunistic” repurchases (outside of 10b5-1 plans) could commence given
recent performance in the stock. Importantly, revenue and margins will
continue to grow/expand sequentially through FY27, which means FCF generation
will also continue to strengthen quarterly. As a result, we model ~$5.6B of
buybacks in FY27 and up to $14B in FY28, followed by $16B of buybacks in FY29
– implying STX can buyback 30% of the company in the next 2.5 years,
conservatively. We believe the direction is clear – STX’s debt reduction phase
is complete, making way for a substantially more buyback-intensive phase for
the foreseeable future (alongside continued dividend increases).

_Beyond our meeting takeaways, we also detail and visualize 3 misconceptions
on the HDD industry that we believe have contributed to recent multiple
compression. Looking forward, (1) strength in fundamentals, (2) elongation of
customer visibility, and (3) clarity on these 3 factors should help the market
re-rate HDD stocks once the storm passes:_

1\. HDDs are critical data center infrastructure in the midst of an
accelerating upcycle, with KPIs signaling continued outperformance. For STX,
nearline EB growth remains one of the clearest forward indicators tied to
share price (Exhibit 2), while for WDC we see a similar relationship between
share price and Q/Q gross profit dollar growth (Exhibit 3). For each company,
both measures are accelerating, yet the consternation around broader AI
spending and HDD market rationality has resulting on STX/WDC diverging from
these historical relationships. Importantly, this is not just a pricing story.
Nearline EB growth is strengthening alongside pricing, reflecting continued
cloud demand, higher-capacity drive adoption and an increasingly data-
intensive workload environment. AI adds another layer of data creation on top
of traditional cloud workloads, reinforcing HDD's role as critical data center
infrastructure rather than simply another component tied to the pace of new
server deployments.

We therefore see an unusual setup – the fundamental indicators that have
historically supported HDD stock outperformance remain intact, while
valuations increasingly discount deterioration ahead. Until we see evidence in
our checks that EB growth, pricing or margins are deteriorating, we believe
these fundamental leading indicators point to higher – not lower – HDD stock
prices.

STX's shares historically have been positively correlated with its nearline EB
shipments, which are expected to grow at a 25%+ CAGR in the coming few years.
 Source: Company data,
Morgan Stanley Research estimates

| | | | | Following several gubernatorial election flips (from Republican to Democratic), and campaigns in many states which featured stricter data center regulation including Texas, Ohio, Nevada, Georgia, and Michigan (D-incumbent), we analyze data center capacity at the state level to help frame risks to the data center buildout.   
---  
| Looking only at under construction data centers, which we view as lower-
risk, we see US data center net additions of 22/24/5 GW-IT for 2027/28/29
(assuming a 1.5 PUE, using Aterio data) compares to our US data center net
addition forecasts of 20/24/23 GW-
IT
and gives us confidence in our forecasts. We believe our forecasts have been
appropriately conservative and recognize that they have likely been below
consensus expectations.  
---  
| Based only on under construction data centers, Texas represents 20% of 2027E
net additions and 27% of 2028E net additions. We focus on Texas as a market
given that the Governor elect has called for an immediate moratorium on data
centers. We note that moratoriums are not bans or cancellations, and believe
the key risks to data center operators are related to delays to ready-for-
service and higher costs.
